channel.title: Worcester Business Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Worcester Business Journal (wbjournal.com)

item.title: 🔒 French defense tech firm undertaking $12M Sturbridge expansion
item.description: This will be the company’s first U.S. manufacturing site for image intensifier tubes used in military night vision equipment.

item.title: Thermo Fisher to lay off 100, close Franklin facility amid executive shakeup
item.description: Biopharma tools and services provider Thermo Fisher Scientific is set to lay off more than 100 workers as the Waltham-based firm is closing its Franklin facility amid an executive shakeup.

item.title: M&T Bank names new regional president for Mass. market
item.description: M&T Bank acquired People’s United Bank, a Connecticut-based chain with offices in Worcester, as part of a $7.6-billion deal in 2021.

item.title: 🔒 Devens manufacturer raises $220M, including from Trump Jr.’s VC firm
item.description: VulcanForms, a Devens-based metal manufacturing company, has secured its second-largest funding round to date, raising $220 million to expand the company’s manufacturing facilities.

item.title: WBJ moves HQ to Downtown Worcester
item.description: After more than three decades on Shrewsbury Street, Worcester Business Journal has moved Downtown.

item.title: Historic Central Mass. properties eligible for $616K in development support

item.title: Checkers set to open in Worcester, brand’s only location in New England, on Feb. 10
item.description: The location replaces a former Honey Dew Donuts at the site, which closed in March.

item.title: 🔒 New England Botanic Garden names new COO
item.description: The Boylston nonprofit has named a replacement for Jane Ellis, who retired from the role this year.

item.title: UMass Chan, Clark, Holy Cross receive Carnegie classifications
item.description: CE Classifications have been awarded to U.S. colleges and universities in rounds for 19 years.

item.title: Mass. open meeting law complaints and violations rose in 2025
item.description: The number of open meeting law complaints and violations reported to the attorney general’s office in 2025 rose above 2024 levels and many more complaints were sent to public bodies directly.
